mcq.q: Space complexity is best defined as:
o: The disk space a program occupies
The amount of memory a program written with a particular algorithm needs to run to completion
The time a program takes to run
The number of variables in the source code
mcq.e: It is about memory needed while the program runs.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a reason to study space complexity?
o: To know whether the available memory is enough
To prefer the program that uses less memory
To estimate the largest problem that can be solved with the available memory
To measure the exact running time in seconds
mcq.e: Running time is time complexity, not space complexity.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a component of space complexity?
mcq.e: The three components are instruction space, data space and environment stack space.

mcq.q: Instruction space depends on:
o: The compiler used, its options and the target architecture
mcq.e: The same source can compile to different amounts of machine code.

mcq.q: Data space is the memory needed for:
o: All constants and variables of the program
mcq.e: Named constants, primitive variables and structured variables all count.

mcq.q: The environment stack keeps:
o: Information needed to resume partially completed functions
mcq.e: Return address, parameters and local variables of active calls.

mcq.q: The environment stack follows which rule?
mcq.e: The most recently called function returns first (LIFO).

mcq.q: If function1 calls function2, what does the environment stack keep so function1 can resume?
o: A pointer to the calling instruction in function1 (return address)
mcq.e: The return address.

mcq.q: Which is an INSENSITIVE factor?
o: A dynamically allocated array of n elements
Stack space of a recursive function
An array whose size depends on n
mcq.e: Primitive variables use the same memory regardless of input.

mcq.q: Which is a SENSITIVE factor?
o: Stack space of a non-recursive function
Stack space of a recursive function
mcq.e: Recursion depth grows with the problem.

mcq.q: In S(n) = c + S_A(n), what is c?
mcq.e: c is the fixed part; S_A(n) varies with the instance characteristic n.

mcq.q: The instance characteristic n is:
o: The total memory of the computer
A number describing the size of the problem instance
The number of lines of code
mcq.e: For example the number of elements in the array.

mcq.q: The iterative sum algorithm (loop with s and i, array passed by REF) has space complexity:
mcq.e: Only primitive variables, the array is passed by reference and there is no recursion, so S_A(n) = 0.

mcq.q: Why is the array a in the iterative sum not counted as sensitive?
o: It is passed by reference so no copy is made by this algorithm
mcq.e: By reference means no extra copy is charged to the algorithm.

mcq.q: The recursive sum(a, n) makes how many calls for a given n (including the base case)?
mcq.e: Calls with n, n-1, ..., 1, 0: that is n + 1 calls.

mcq.q: On a 32-bit machine each call of the recursive sum keeps n (4 bytes), a (4 bytes) and a return address (4 bytes). Total stack for n = 9?
mcq.e: 12 bytes x (9 + 1) = 120 bytes.

mcq.q: Which statement compares the two sum algorithms correctly?
o: The recursive one uses O(n) stack space; the iterative one uses O(1)
The iterative one uses O(n) space; the recursive one O(1)
mcq.e: Recursion keeps a frame per pending call.

mcq.q: int arr[n]; uses 40 bytes when n = 10. How many bytes when n = 1000 (int = 4 bytes)?
mcq.e: 1000 x 4 = 4000 bytes: the memory changes with input, so it is sensitive.

mcq.q: A function that recursively computes factorial of n has which kind of environment stack contribution?
mcq.e: Recursive functions are a sensitive factor.

mcq.q: A program that sorts an array of n integers has which kind of data space contribution from the array?
mcq.e: Structured variables whose size depends on n are sensitive.

mcq.q: Which is true about the instruction space contribution?
mcq.e: Instruction space is listed among the insensitive factors.

mcq.q: For a loop 'for (i = 0; i < n; i++)' that creates no additional variables, the overall space complexity is:
mcq.e: Only one variable i is used regardless of n.

written.q: Define space complexity and state three reasons for being interested in it.
written.a: Space complexity is the amount of memory a program written with a particular algorithm needs to run to its completion. We care because: (1) we want to know whether the available memory is enough to run the program; (2) we prefer the program that consumes less memory when several algorithms solve a problem; (3) we can estimate the largest problem our algorithm can solve with the memory available.

written.q: Name the components of space complexity and state what each depends on.
written.a: Instruction space: compiler used, compiler options, architecture of the target computer. Data space: data types and the number of named constants, primitive variables and structured variables. Environment stack space: the information (return addresses, parameters, local variables) kept for functions that have been called but not yet completed; depends on call structure and recursion.

written.q: Distinguish sensitive and insensitive factors with examples.
written.a: Insensitive: instruction space; data space from literal constants, named constants and primitive variables; stack space from non-recursive functions. Sensitive: data space from structured variables and dynamic memory allocation (e.g. sorting an array of n integers); stack space from recursive functions (e.g. recursive factorial). Space complexity: S(n) = c + SA(n), where c is the insensitive part and SA(n) the sensitive part.

written.q: Analyse the space complexity of the iterative sum(REF a[], n) (loop with variables s and i).
written.a: n, s and i are primitive variables: insensitive. The array a is passed by reference, so no copy is made for this algorithm: insensitive. The algorithm is non-recursive, so its stack space is insensitive. Hence SA(n) = 0 and S(n) = c: constant space, O(1).

written.q: Analyse the recursive sum(REF a[], n) on a 32-bit machine and compare it with the iterative version.
written.a: n and a[] are insensitive (primitive, passed by reference), but the environment stack is sensitive because of recursion. Each call keeps n (4 bytes), a (4 bytes) and the return address (4 bytes) = 12 bytes. There are n + 1 calls, so stack space is about 12(n + 1) bytes: S(n) grows linearly, O(n). The iterative version needs only constant space, so it is the better choice when memory is limited.
